title: Club Membership
subtitle: Members, dependents, plans and renewals
summary: Club Membership handles applications, activation, dependents, plan changes and yearly renewals, and answers one question for the rest of the club: is this person a member in good standing today, and how many guests may they bring?

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: A member is a party with a plan (FULL, SOCIAL, JUNIOR) and a membership year. Activation creates and invoices the first year; renewals are generated in bulk for members within RENEWAL_LEAD_DAYS of expiry, invoiced together, and marked paid, waived or deleted while still DUE.
Every fee becomes an AR invoice through the AR import, and marking a renewal paid here settles that invoice: the member desk never has to touch the receivables screen.
Hospitality calls the standing API before every reservation and event booking, so suspending a member takes effect in the restaurant immediately.

sections.title: Membership database architecture · Visual ERD
sections.intro: The membership schema has four business tables and six declared foreign keys. The diagram separates domain-owned membership data from the shared party and legal-entity master records.

sections.title: Club Membership explained in everyday language
items: The plan is the product. The club defines what a FULL, SOCIAL or JUNIOR-style membership costs, its currency and its guest allowance in membership_plan. Those names are examples from the Academy; actual plans are configurable.
The member is a person or organisation with a relationship to the club. club_member connects the common party record to a plan, a membership number and its current lifecycle status.
Dependents are not just text fields. member_dependent references another registered party, preserving identity across other club services.
Renewal is a repeatable financial obligation. membership_renewal tracks the period, amount, and whether it is due, invoiced, paid or waived.

Good standing is a business decision. An ACTIVE status alone may not be enough: the service must also consider expiry, suspension and any applicable standing policy at the time it answers Hospitality.

sections.title: All six declared database relationships
sections.intro: Every arrow corresponds to a real foreign-key constraint in the uploaded SQL. Parent records may have many children; each non-null foreign key requires a matching parent.

Membership points to a shared business party; UNIQUE(party_id) limits each party to one member record.

Avoids ambiguity between plan codes for one club entity.
Only one member row per party
This schema represents one membership record per shared party.
Prevents duplicate dependent registrations for the same member.
Renewal date range and fee validity
End cannot precede start; fee cannot be negative.
Partly — ENUM restricts status values; business checks are separate
Timing, payment, and suspension policy need service logic.
Invoices, payment collection and GL posting
No — not enforced by these four tables

sections.title: Design decisions
items: Standing is computed, not stored, and served over REST so every consumer sees the same answer.
Overlapping renewal periods and edits to invoiced renewals are blocked in the database.
